name_en: Digital arrest (fake police/CBI/ED video-call custody)
summary: Callers posing as police, CBI, Narcotics, ED, RBI, customs or judges tell the victim that they (or a relative) are linked to drugs, money laundering or a seized parcel, then keep the victim on a continuous Skype/WhatsApp video call ('digital arrest') in isolation. Using fake uniforms, police-station studios and forged court/ED orders, they demand money as 'bail', settlement, or for 'verification' of funds that will supposedly be returned, often moved by RTGS from broken FDs and savings.
victim_profile: People of every class and age group (PM, Mann Ki Baat 2024); senior citizens are repeatedly named among victims by the Supreme Court and in bank-intervention cases.
indicators: unsolicited call or video call from someone claiming to be police/CBI/ED/narcotics/RBI
claims of drugs, fake passports or money laundering linked to your Aadhaar, phone or parcel
told to stay on camera continuously and not leave the room or tell anyone
fake arrest warrants, court or ED orders sent on WhatsApp
demand to transfer savings or break FDs for 'verification' or 'bail' with a promise of refund
caller stays on the line while you are at the bank branch
typical_claims: your parcel contains drugs and fake passports and has been seized
a money-laundering case is registered against your Aadhaar
you are under digital arrest until the investigation is complete
transfer your funds to an RBI/government account for verification; it will be returned
decide now or you will be arrested
coaching_phrases: stay on the video call and do not disconnect
isolate yourself and do not tell anyone, including family
keep the matter confidential because it is a secret investigation
move your money to the given account for verification; it will be refunded
give the bank a personal reason (e.g. buying property) when breaking FDs (observed: victim gave this reason while fraudsters stayed on the phone)
stay under 'digital custody' at home and do not speak to family; ignore bank staff who question the transfer (reported pattern among senior victims)
red_flag_questions: Is anyone on a call or video call with you right now asking you to make this payment?
Has someone said you are under investigation or arrest by police, CBI, ED or narcotics?
Were you told to keep this secret from your family or the bank?
Were you told this money will be returned after it is 'verified'?
Did you receive a warrant or court order on WhatsApp?
cues_en: they said i am under arrest
cues_hinglish: aapka aadhaar crime mein use hua
paise verify karke wapas kar denge
police wale video call pe the
cues_hi: आपके नाम पर केस दर्ज है
पैसे वेरिफिकेशन के बाद लौटा देंगे
आपका आधार अपराध में इस्तेमाल हुआ

first_seen.value: by 2022 (MHA data starts 2022; MHA alert May 2024)

trend.note: Per MoS Home written reply (reported by Outlook Money, Mar 2025): 39,925 cases/Rs 91.14 cr (2022), 60,676/Rs 339.03 cr (2023), 1,23,672/Rs 1935.51 cr (2024). Supreme Court (Nov 2025) cited about Rs 3,000 crore extorted.

official_truth: There is no such thing as a 'digital arrest' under Indian law; police, CBI, ED, customs and judges never arrest, investigate or demand money over a phone or video call, and RBI does not hold 'verification' accounts for individuals.
advice: Stop, think, take action: disconnect the call and do not pay
Tell a family member and verify with your local police station
Call 1930 or report at cybercrime.gov.in immediately
Never move savings to any 'verification' or 'safe' account
applicability_note: Victim personally initiates large RTGS/IMPS/UPI transfers (often after breaking FDs) while on a call, exactly the payment Ruko can hold and call back on.

name_en: Courier / parcel scam (FedEx-style drug parcel and fake India Post redelivery)
summary: A caller posing as a courier company (often 'FedEx') says a parcel in the victim's name containing drugs, passports or contraband has been seized, then 'transfers' the call to fake customs/Mumbai Police/narcotics officers on Skype or WhatsApp, who demand money for 'verification' or to settle the case; this usually escalates into a digital arrest. A lighter SMS variant impersonates India Post, claiming delivery failed due to an incomplete address and sending a link to 'update' details or pay a small redelivery fee.
victim_profile: General public; documented cases include salaried professionals such as software engineers in Bengaluru (TNM 2024).
indicators: automated or live call about a parcel you never sent
parcel 'seized' at airport with drugs, passports or contraband
call transferred to customs, narcotics or Mumbai police
asked to install Skype or join a video call for a 'statement'
told to pay into an RBI/verification account with refund promised
SMS saying delivery failed and asking to update address via a link
typical_claims: a parcel in your name with drugs and passports was seized at Mumbai airport
your Aadhaar was used to send this parcel to Taiwan
I am transferring your call to Mumbai police/customs
transfer the amount for RBI verification; it will be refunded in 30 days
your package could not be delivered due to incomplete address; update within 24 hours
coaching_phrases: take the calls from an isolated room with your camera on
transfer money to the 'RBI' account for verification; it will be returned within 30 days
red_flag_questions: Did someone call you about a parcel or courier you did not send?
Were you transferred from a courier company to a police or customs officer?
Are you being asked to pay to clear your name or for 'verification'?
Did an SMS ask you to click a link to update a delivery address or pay a redelivery fee?
cues_en: they said my parcel had drugs
cues_hinglish: aapke naam ka parcel pakda gaya
aapka aadhaar parcel mein use hua
cues_hi: आपके नाम का पार्सल पकड़ा गया

first_seen.value: 2023 (FedEx variant came to the fore that year, per Deccan Herald)

trend.note: Deccan Herald reported 111 FedEx courier scam cases registered up to Nov 2023; the parcel script remains a standard opener named in the MHA May 2024 digital-arrest alert; PIB Fact Check debunked India Post address SMS again in Jan 2026.

official_truth: Courier companies and India Post do not call or message you to settle seized-parcel cases or ask you to update an address via a link, and police never investigate or collect money over Skype or video calls.
advice: Hang up and check the tracking number only on the courier's official website
Never pay to 'clear' a parcel case or for verification
Do not click delivery links in SMS; delete them
Report to 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in
applicability_note: Fake-police variant leads the victim to push large RTGS/IMPS transfers that Ruko can hold; the India Post SMS variant is mainly card/data phishing (partial).

name_en: SIM / mobile number disconnection threat (fake DoT/TRAI)
summary: An automated or live call claiming to be from DoT or TRAI says the victim's mobile number will be blocked within hours because a SIM taken on their Aadhaar was used for illegal activity, harassment or fraud. The victim is told to 'press 9', is given a fake FIR number and is transferred to fake police/CBI, which commonly escalates into a digital arrest with demands for fines, bail or 'verification' transfers; the call is also used to harvest Aadhaar and bank details.
victim_profile: General public; documented victims include retirees (e.g. a retired Air Force employee in Faridabad, PTI via Deccan Herald, Nov 2024).
indicators: IVR call saying your number will be blocked in two hours
asked to press 9 to speak to a TRAI or DoT officer
claim that a SIM issued on your Aadhaar was used for crime or harassment
caller gives an FIR number and transfers you to police or CBI
WhatsApp call from a foreign number (e.g. +92) posing as an official
demand for a penalty or verification payment to keep the number active
typical_claims: your mobile number will be disconnected within two hours
another SIM in your name is being used for illegal activities
a complaint/FIR is registered against your number
you need a police clarification letter to keep your number
I am transferring you to the cyber crime police
coaching_phrases: do not disconnect the call or action will be taken against your family (reported in the Faridabad digital-arrest case that began with a fake TRAI call)
red_flag_questions: Did someone say your mobile number or SIM will be blocked?
Did they say they were from TRAI or DoT and then transfer you to police?
Were you asked to pay a fine or 'verification' amount to keep your number?
Is the caller still on the line asking you to make this payment?
cues_en: they said my sim is being misused
cues_hinglish: aapke aadhaar pe dusra sim liya gaya
police complaint hai aapke number pe
police se clarification letter lana hoga
cues_hi: आपका नंबर दो घंटे में बंद हो जाएगा

trend.note: TRAI data cited by Kerala Kaumudi (Apr 2026): spam-call complaints rose from 13.62 lakh (2023) to 19.38 lakh (2024) and 31.09 lakh (2025); not specific to disconnection calls.

official_truth: DoT and TRAI never call citizens to threaten disconnection and have authorised no one to do so; disconnections for KYC or misuse are handled only by your own telecom operator.
advice: Hang up; verify only with your operator's official customer care
Check connections in your name on Sanchar Saathi and report the call on Chakshu
Never pay to keep a number active
Call 1930 if money has been lost
applicability_note: Often the opener of a digital arrest where the victim later pushes transfers Ruko can hold; on its own it is mostly data harvesting.

name_en: KYC / PAN / Aadhaar update 'account will be blocked' scam
summary: SMS, WhatsApp or calls in the name of a bank (often SBI/YONO), wallet or telco say the account, card or SIM will be blocked, frozen or closed today unless KYC, PAN or Aadhaar is updated via a link, a phone call or a KYC-named APK. The link or app harvests login, card and OTP details or gives remote control, after which money is drained; callers may also push screen-sharing apps or ask for a small 'KYC fee' payment.
victim_profile: General public; RBI aims its warnings especially at those new to digital banking (BE(A)WARE preface). No specific profile documented.
indicators: message says account/YONO/card will be blocked or closed today
link or APK file sent to 'update KYC', PAN or Aadhaar
sender is a mobile number rather than an official short code
caller asks for OTP, card details or to install a screen-sharing app
false urgency or threat of account freezing
typical_claims: your SBI YONO account is closed today; update your PAN now
your account will be blocked as your KYC has expired
install this KYC app to avoid losing services
your Aadhaar details are incomplete; update immediately
share the OTP to complete KYC verification
red_flag_questions: Did you get a message saying your account or card will be blocked unless you update KYC, PAN or Aadhaar?
Did you install any app or APK, or click a link, sent by SMS or WhatsApp?
Has anyone asked you to share an OTP or install a screen-sharing app?
Is someone guiding you on the phone right now?
cues_en: they said my account will be frozen
cues_hinglish: kyc update karo warna account band
ye app download karo kyc ke liye
link pe click karke update karo
sim band ho jayega kyc nahi hua

first_seen.value: by September 2021 (first RBI caution on KYC-updation frauds)

trend.note: RBI re-issued its caution in Feb 2024 citing continuing incidents; Delhi Police found more than 100 cases in one fake-YONO network (Moneylife, Sep 2022); PIB Fact Check flagged an APK-based SBI YONO Aadhaar variant in March 2026.

official_truth: RBI says that for any KYC update request you should contact your bank directly through its official website or branch; banks do not ask you to update KYC through links, APK files or by sharing OTPs.
advice: Do not click KYC links or install APKs from SMS/WhatsApp
Visit the branch or use the bank's official app to check KYC status
Never share OTP, PIN or card details
Report to 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in and inform your bank at once
applicability_note: Money usually leaves via stolen credentials, OTPs or a malicious app rather than a victim-initiated transfer; Ruko can warn but rarely hold.

name_en: Electricity bill disconnection threat
summary: An SMS or WhatsApp message from a personal mobile number claims the consumer's power will be cut tonight (often '9:30 pm') because last month's bill was not updated, and asks them to call an 'electricity officer'. The caller asks for a token payment (documented amounts include Re 1 and Rs 100) to 'update the entry' and gets the victim to install a remote-access app such as Quick Support or AnyDesk, then uses the captured banking/card details to drain the account.
victim_profile: General public; documented victims include senior citizens and retirees (Tribune, Jalandhar 2022).
indicators: message from a 10-digit mobile number, not the discom's sender ID
threat that power will be cut tonight at a specific time
asked to call an 'electricity officer' on a personal number
asked to pay a small token amount to update the bill
asked to install Quick Support, AnyDesk or another app
typical_claims: your electricity will be disconnected tonight at 9:30 pm
your previous month's bill was not updated
call the electricity officer immediately on this number
pay re 1 / rs 100 to update your previous entry
download this app so I can update your bill
coaching_phrases: install the remote support app the 'officer' names and keep the call going while making the small payment
red_flag_questions: Did you get a message saying your electricity will be cut tonight?
Did the message come from a normal mobile number and ask you to call an officer?
Have you been asked to install an app like AnyDesk or Quick Support?
Are you paying a small amount through a link the caller sent?
cues_en: they said my light will be cut
cues_hinglish: aaj raat bijli kaat di jayegi
bijli ka bill update nahi hua
pichle mahine ka bill pending hai
ye app download karo bill ke liye
bijli vibhag se bol raha hoon
cues_hi: आज रात बिजली काट दी जाएगी

trend.note: Repeated discom warnings from Punjab (2022), Telangana (2023) and Maharashtra (May 2026); no cited statistics.

official_truth: Electricity distribution companies do not message you from personal mobile numbers, send payment links, or ask you to install apps; pay bills only through the discom's official app, website or office.
advice: Do not call the number in the message
Never install remote-access apps on a caller's request
Check your bill on the official discom app/website or call the discom helpline
Report to 1930 if money was lost
applicability_note: The victim makes a small initial payment Ruko could flag, but the large losses usually come via remote-access takeover rather than victim-pushed transfers.

name_en: Fake traffic e-challan / RTO / Parivahan link or APK
summary: SMS or WhatsApp messages carrying realistic traffic-violation details claim an e-challan is pending and send a link to a cloned Parivahan/MVD portal or an APK named like 'RTO Challan' or 'e Challan App'. The fake site collects card/UPI details for the 'fine', while the APK grabs SMS and OTPs, takes over WhatsApp, forwards itself to contacts, and is used to drain bank or e-commerce accounts. Newer APKs (e.g. 'MParivahan.apk') install a hidden second app that overlays fake banking screens; CERT-In has alerted on this campaign (Moneylife, Mar 2026).
victim_profile: Vehicle owners; general public. CloudSEK found Gujarat and Karnataka most affected (IANS 2024).
indicators: challan message from a private mobile number or WhatsApp
link that is not echallan.parivahan.gov.in or the state MVD site
asked to download an APK file to view or pay the challan
site asks for vehicle number then shows a fake security check
new app asks for SMS, contacts and default-messaging permissions
typical_claims: your vehicle has a pending traffic e-challan
pay your fine today to avoid court action
download the RTO challan app to see the violation
your challan details are attached; click to view
pay the challan online through this link
red_flag_questions: Did you receive a traffic challan on WhatsApp or SMS with a link or an app file?
Did you install any app to view or pay the challan?
Is the payment page the official Parivahan e-challan site you typed yourself?
Have you received OTPs you did not request since then?

trend.note: CloudSEK (IANS, Jul 2024) counted over 4,400 infected devices; police warnings continued into 2026 (Kerala Police, Sep 2026).

official_truth: Genuine e-challan payment or verification never requires downloading an APK; check challans only on the official Parivahan/MVD portal by typing the address yourself.
advice: Never install APK files sent by SMS/WhatsApp
Check challans by typing echallan.parivahan.gov.in yourself
If installed: go offline, uninstall, check bank/UPI and change passwords from another device
Report to 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in
applicability_note: Losses come from malware/OTP interception and fake payment pages rather than a victim-pushed transfer Ruko can hold; Ruko can mainly warn.

name_en: Fake income tax refund / tax notice / penalty
summary: Emails, SMS, WhatsApp messages or calls posing as the Income Tax Department claim a refund is approved (e.g. a Rs 60,000 refund needing 'manual verification'), or that a demand, penalty or prosecution notice is pending with a short deadline, and send a link or file. The link leads to a cloned portal that captures PAN, net-banking passwords, card data and OTPs, or delivers OTP-stealing malware; the department says its communications never contain hyperlinks.
victim_profile: Taxpayers; general public. No specific profile documented in cited sources.
indicators: email or SMS about a tax refund or notice that contains a link
refund 'approved' but you must verify or update bank/card details
sender address or domain that is not incometax.gov.in
request for net-banking password, card number or OTP to receive a refund
threat of penalty or legal action unless paid immediately
typical_claims: you are eligible for a refund of Rs 60,000; verify manually through this link
Income Tax Department | Important Message: view message on e-filing portal
a tax demand is outstanding; submit documents within 72 hours or face prosecution
your tax payment is frozen; pay the challan through this link
download your instant e-PAN card
red_flag_questions: Did you receive a refund or tax notice message with a link?
Were you asked to enter net-banking, card details or an OTP to get a refund?
Are you being asked to pay a tax penalty to a personal account or via a link?
Have you checked the notice by logging in to incometax.gov.in yourself?
cues_en: they said my refund is stuck
cues_hinglish: bank details verify karo refund ke liye
link pe click karke refund lo
tax ka challan link se bharo

first_seen.value: by 2016 (department has warned about phishing emails since 2016, per Moneylife)

trend.note: Moneylife (Aug 2026) documents multiple new PIB-flagged I-T phishing variants (demand, penalty, refund, e-PAN) and CloudSEK-reported malware penalty notices; the e-Filing portal carries a scam banner (Aug 2026). No cited statistics.

official_truth: Official Income Tax Department communications never contain hyperlinks, and refunds are credited only to a bank account you validate yourself after logging in to incometax.gov.in.
advice: Do not click links in refund or notice messages
Check refund/notice status only by logging in at incometax.gov.in yourself
Never share net-banking passwords, card details or OTPs
Report to 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in
applicability_note: Mainly credential phishing where fraudsters move the money themselves; Ruko can warn but only holds if the victim is induced to pay a 'penalty'.

name_en: Fake government scheme / subsidy registration fee
summary: Fraudsters advertise or message about government schemes (e.g. PM-KUSUM solar pumps, free laptops, free solar flour mills, government loans) through look-alike websites, WhatsApp forwards and calls, then collect Aadhaar, bank details and an upfront 'registration', 'processing' or 'legal insurance' fee, sometimes promising it is refundable. Some variants push links or apps that harvest data; the benefit never arrives.
victim_profile: Farmers (PM-KUSUM solar pump fraud), rural women (solar flour mill offer), students (laptop scheme) and loan seekers, per Moneylife reports of PIB/ministry warnings.
indicators: scheme promoted via WhatsApp forward or a non-.gov.in website
upfront registration, processing or insurance fee to receive a subsidy or benefit
promise that the fee will be refunded
request for Aadhaar, bank details or OTP to 'register'
forged approval letter on government letterhead
typical_claims: you are eligible for a solar pump under PM-KUSUM; pay the registration amount
register now for the free laptop scheme
your government loan of Rs 3 lakh is approved; pay the legal insurance charge
the registration fee is refundable after installation
limited seats, apply today
red_flag_questions: Is this payment a fee to get a government scheme, subsidy or loan?
Did you find the scheme through a WhatsApp message, social media ad or a non-government website?
Were you told the fee will be refunded later?
Has anyone asked for your Aadhaar, bank details or an OTP to register?
cues_en: they said i will get subsidy
cues_hinglish: aadhaar number bhejo yojana ke liye

first_seen.value: by 2022 (MNRE warning on fake PM-KUSUM portals)

trend.note: New scheme hoaxes continue to be flagged by PIB Fact Check (Moneylife, Oct 2025); RBI lists 'social welfare scheme fraud' among its forty stories. No cited statistics.

official_truth: Government schemes are verified only on official .gov.in portals, and genuine schemes do not ask you to pay registration or processing fees to private accounts or share OTPs.
advice: Verify the scheme on the ministry's .gov.in site or india.gov.in
Never pay a fee to receive a subsidy or benefit
Do not share Aadhaar, bank details or OTP on forwarded links
Report to 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in
applicability_note: The victim personally pays the registration/processing fee by UPI or transfer, which Ruko can hold and question.

name_en: EPFO / PF withdrawal or claim 'processing fee'
summary: People seeking PF withdrawals, transfers, KYC corrections or claim settlement are approached by 'agents', cyber-cafe operators, fintech intermediaries or look-alike EPFO/labour-ministry portals that charge fees for services EPFO provides free, or collect UAN, Aadhaar, bank and OTP details. EPFO warns this exposes members' financial data; RBI also documents fake helpline numbers planted in search results that ask callers for card or account details.
victim_profile: EPFO members, employers and pensioners (EPFO press release, Jun 2025); no further profile documented.
indicators: someone offers to speed up a PF claim or withdrawal for a fee
request for UAN password, Aadhaar OTP or bank details by phone or WhatsApp
EPFO 'helpline' number found via search engine or social media
website or app that is not epfindia.gov.in / UMANG claiming to be EPFO or a labour-ministry scheme
demand to pay before the claim is released
typical_claims: your PF claim is stuck; pay a processing fee to release it
I can get your PF withdrawn today for a charge
share the OTP to update your KYC on the EPFO portal
register on this portal for the government employment scheme
red_flag_questions: Is this payment a fee to get your PF claim, withdrawal or KYC done?
Who gave you this number or website: EPFO's official site, or a search result or social media?
Has anyone asked for your UAN password or an Aadhaar OTP?
Did they promise faster settlement if you pay?
cues_hinglish: kyc update karna padega pf ka

trend.note: EPFO issued a caution against paid intermediaries in June 2025 and the Labour Ministry disowned fake scheme portals in Sept 2025; no impersonation statistics found.

official_truth: All EPFO services, including claims, transfers, KYC updates and grievances, are entirely free through the EPFO portal and UMANG app, and members should not pay any fee to agents or third parties.
advice: Use only the EPFO member portal, UMANG app or an EPFO office/helpdesk
Never pay anyone to release or speed up a PF claim
Never share UAN password or Aadhaar OTP
Report fraud to 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in
applicability_note: Fee payments to 'agents' are victim-initiated and holdable; credential/OTP theft variants are not. Direct EPFO-impersonation call evidence was thin in sources reachable in this run.

name_en: Fake scholarship sanction / processing fee
summary: Pattern as scoped for Ruko: students or parents are told by call, SMS or WhatsApp that a government scholarship or student benefit has been sanctioned and must be 'released' after paying a processing/registration fee or sharing bank details and OTPs. Evidence status: no source fetched in this run documented this exact script; documented neighbours are PIB-flagged student-benefit hoaxes such as a fake 'Students' Laptop Scheme 2025' phishing link, and the general rule that genuine schemes never charge registration or processing fees.
victim_profile: Students and their parents (inferred from the scheme type; no source in this run profiles victims).
indicators: unsolicited message saying a scholarship is sanctioned
fee demanded to release or process the scholarship
link that is not scholarships.gov.in or a state .gov.in portal
request for bank details, Aadhaar or OTP by phone
deadline pressure to pay today
typical_claims: your scholarship has been approved; pay the processing fee to receive it
register on this link for the student scheme
share the OTP to link your bank account for the scholarship amount
red_flag_questions: Is this payment a fee to receive a scholarship or student benefit?
Did the offer come by call, SMS or WhatsApp rather than from the National Scholarship Portal?
Has anyone asked for an OTP or bank details to 'release' the amount?
Did you apply for this scholarship yourself on the official portal?
cues_en: they said my child got a scholarship
cues_hinglish: scholarship ka paisa release karna hai

trend.note: No statistics or dated advisory found in this run.

official_truth: Central scholarships are applied for on the National Scholarship Portal, where assisted applications at Common Service Centres cost a fixed Rs 30 in total, and genuine government schemes do not ask for registration or processing fees or OTPs over the phone.
advice: Check status only on scholarships.gov.in or the state portal
Never pay a fee to 'release' a scholarship
Never share OTP or bank login details
Report to 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in
applicability_note: If it occurs as scoped, the parent or student pays the fee themselves, which Ruko can hold; documentation of this exact script was not reachable in this run (low confidence).

name_en: Fake gas agency / LPG KYC / PNG disconnection / dealership
summary: Messages in the name of LPG companies or city-gas utilities say an LPG booking needs renewal or KYC update to keep cylinder deliveries, or that piped gas will be cut tonight at 9:30 pm unless the bill is updated. Victims are asked to call a number, pay a small 'system update' fee and install an APK such as 'Gas Bill Update.apk' or 'BILL_UPDATE.apk', which captures banking credentials; a separate variant sends forged LPG distributorship/dealership letters demanding fees.
victim_profile: Household gas consumers; documented Mahanagar Gas victims include a 75-year-old retiree (Moneylife, Jun 2026); dealership variant targets would-be distributors.
indicators: WhatsApp message with gas company logo from a personal number
threat that gas supply will be cut tonight (e.g. 9:30 pm)
LPG booking 'renewal' or KYC update needed via link
request for a Rs 10 'system update' fee, then 'payment not received'
APK file named like a bill or gas update
dealership offer letter asking for registration or security fees
typical_claims: your gas connection will be disconnected tonight at 9:30 pm
update your LPG KYC to continue cylinder delivery
pay Rs 10 to update the system
your payment did not reflect; install this app to complete it
you have been selected for an LPG distributorship
coaching_phrases: stay on the call while installing the 'bill update' app and entering bank details (victim kept on phone for 45 minutes in one Mumbai case)
red_flag_questions: Did you get a message that your gas supply or LPG connection will be cut or needs KYC?
Was it from a regular mobile number rather than the company's official app or number?
Have you been asked to install an app or APK to pay or update the bill?
Is this payment a fee for an LPG dealership or distributorship?
cues_en: they said my gas will be cut
cues_hinglish: aaj raat gas band ho jayegi
ye app install karo bill ke liye

first_seen.value: by 2025 (PIB-flagged fake LPG dealership letters reported Oct 2025); PNG disconnection wave from March 2026

trend.note: Moneylife (Jun 2026): more than 130 Mahanagar Gas customers reportedly targeted since late March with about Rs 3 crore lost; LPG KYC/booking APK messages reported during a shortage (Moneylife, Mar 2026).

official_truth: Gas companies do not ask for OTPs, bank details or app installs over calls or WhatsApp; LPG bookings and KYC should be done only through the oil company's official app or portal, and LPG distributorship applications only via lpgvitarakchayan.in.
advice: Do not call numbers or install apps from gas-bill messages
Check bills and KYC only on the company's official app/website or distributor
Never pay fees for an LPG dealership outside the official portal
If an APK was installed: go offline, uninstall, change UPI PIN/passwords and call 1930
applicability_note: Small fee payments and dealership fees are victim-initiated and holdable, but large losses usually come from APK-based account takeover.

name_en: Fake insurance bonus / maturity / lapsed-policy revival (IRDAI/LIC/RBI impersonation)
summary: Callers posing as insurance company staff, IRDAI or even RBI officials tell policyholders that a policy has matured or earned a large bonus, refund or revival benefit, then demand 'processing fees', charges or taxes before release and keep escalating demands. Variants use fake IRDAI complaint/grievance websites that collect policy, bank and OTP details or payments, and fake insurance call centres selling discounted renewals.
victim_profile: Policyholders, including elderly retirees (e.g. an 82-year-old retired professor in Delhi, Moneylife 2022).
indicators: unsolicited call about a large policy bonus, maturity amount or refund
caller claims to be from IRDAI, RBI or the insurer's head office
fee, tax or charge demanded before the payout is released
repeated new charges after each payment
complaint or claim website that is not bimabharosa.irdai.gov.in or the insurer's site
typical_claims: your policies have matured and you are eligible for a Rs 90 lakh bonus
pay a processing fee to release your bonus
your lapsed policy can be revived with full benefits if you pay now
register your complaint here to get your refund
I am a senior official from RBI handling your insurance payout
red_flag_questions: Has someone told you a policy bonus, maturity amount or refund will be released after you pay a fee?
Did the caller claim to be from IRDAI, RBI or a head office rather than your insurer's branch?
Have you been asked to pay again after an earlier payment?
Did you verify this by calling the insurer's official number yourself?
cues_hinglish: bonus release karne ke liye fees
cues_hi: बोनस जारी करने के लिए शुल्क

trend.note: IRDAI issued a fresh caution against fake grievance websites in Sept 2026; no cited statistics.

official_truth: IRDAI warns the public not to make payments or share policy, bank or OTP details in response to websites, messages or calls misusing its name, and to register insurance complaints only on the official Bima Bharosa portal.
advice: Never pay a fee to receive a bonus, maturity or refund
Verify by calling your insurer's official number from the policy document
Register complaints only at bimabharosa.irdai.gov.in
Report to 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in
applicability_note: Victims personally transfer repeated 'fees' and charges, which Ruko can hold and question.

name_en: Fake bank fraud team: 'block the unauthorised transaction', share OTP or move money to a safe/RBI account
summary: A caller posing as the bank's fraud, security or card department (sometimes quoting the customer's name or date of birth) says there is an unauthorised transaction or the account will be frozen, and to 'block' or 'reverse' it the customer must share an OTP/PIN/CVV or install a screen-sharing app and type in card details. A related script, seen in digital-arrest cases, asks victims to move funds to an 'RBI' or verification account for safekeeping; RBI holds no accounts for individuals, so such transfers go straight to mule accounts.
victim_profile: General public; senior citizens are frequently targeted with account-freeze calls (Moneylife, Apr 2026).
indicators: unsolicited call about an unauthorised transaction or account freeze
caller already knows your name or date of birth to sound genuine
asks for OTP, PIN or CVV to 'block' or 'reverse' a transaction
asks you to install a screen-sharing or support app and type in card details
asks you to transfer money to a 'safe', 'secure' or RBI account
call not from the number printed on your card or the bank's official 1600-series number
typical_claims: we have detected an unauthorised transaction on your account
your account will be frozen unless you verify now
share the OTP you just received so we can block the transaction
install this app so our team can secure your account
move your balance to this safe account until the issue is fixed
coaching_phrases: type the card details and OTP into the app yourself instead of reading them out (screen-sharing variant)
red_flag_questions: Did someone from the 'bank' call you first about a suspicious transaction?
Were you asked to move money to another account to keep it safe?
Has anyone asked you to install an app or share an OTP to block or reverse a transaction?
Did you call back on the number printed on your card or the bank's website?
cues_en: they said someone is using my card
cues_hinglish: aapke account se galat transaction hua hai
otp batao block karne ke liye
paise safe account mein daal do
fraud department se bol raha hoon

trend.note: Still described as a common account-drain method against seniors (Moneylife, Apr 2026); no cited statistics specific to this variant.

official_truth: Banks, RBI and other genuine entities never ask for OTP, PIN, CVV or passwords, banks never ask you to install third-party apps, and RBI does not hold accounts for individuals, so any 'safe account' is a fraudster's account.
advice: Hang up and call the number on the back of your card or the bank's website
Never share OTP/PIN/CVV or install apps on a caller's request
Never move money to a 'safe' account
Report at once to your bank and 1930
applicability_note: 'Safe account' transfers are victim-pushed and holdable; OTP/screen-sharing variants let fraudsters move money themselves, so Ruko can only warn.

name_en: Credit card reward points redemption / expiry lure
summary: Messages or calls in a card issuer's name offer to redeem or 'save' expiring reward points or cashback through a link, form or app; the link or APK captures card number, CVV, OTPs and SMS, and fraudsters then make card or e-commerce transactions. Note: the sources reachable in this run document these mechanics under card-offer, cashback and bank-SMS APK pretexts; no fetched source described the reward-points wording specifically.
victim_profile: Credit card holders; no specific profile documented in cited sources.
indicators: message saying reward points or cashback will expire today
link or APK to 'redeem' points or claim an offer
form asking for card number, expiry, CVV or OTP
sender is a mobile number or unofficial WhatsApp account
OTPs arriving for purchases you did not make
typical_claims: your reward points worth a large amount expire today; redeem now
download this app to convert your points to cash
fill this form to claim your card benefit
share the OTP to credit the points to your account
red_flag_questions: Did a message or call offer to redeem reward points or cashback through a link or app?
Did you enter card details, CVV or an OTP on that link or app?
Did you install any app or file sent on WhatsApp or SMS?
Are OTPs or purchase alerts arriving that you did not start?
cues_en: they said my points will lapse
cues_hinglish: reward points expire ho rahe hain
ye app download karo points ke liye
otp batao points credit karne ke liye

trend.note: No statistics or dated reward-points-specific advisory reached in this run; related card-offer APK fraud reported Nov 2025.

official_truth: Card issuers never ask you to install third-party apps or share OTP, CVV or PIN; malicious APKs shared over SMS, email or WhatsApp are used to steal card details.
advice: Check and redeem points only in the issuer's official app or website
Never open APK files or links from SMS/WhatsApp
Never share CVV, OTP or PIN
Block the card and call 1930 if details were entered
applicability_note: Card data/OTP theft lets fraudsters transact without a victim-initiated transfer; Ruko can only warn. Evidence for the exact reward-points wording was not reachable in this run.

name_en: Credit card limit increase / annual fee waiver / activation / new card offer
summary: Callers or messages posing as the card issuer or an NBFC offer a credit limit enhancement, annual-fee waiver, card activation help or a new premium/lifetime-free card, and ask the customer to call a mobile number, fill a 'form', open a link or install an app, then share OTP/PIN or approve a token Re 1 payment. The captured details or malicious APK are used for unauthorised card and account transactions.
victim_profile: Credit card holders and applicants; documented cases include a businessman in Andheri (Moneylife 2022) and a frequent flyer lured by a Facebook lounge-access card ad (Moneylife 2025).
indicators: unsolicited offer to raise your credit limit or waive the annual fee
caller asks you to fill a form sent on WhatsApp or install an app/APK
asked to share OTP, CVV or approve a Re 1 payment to 'verify'
contact number is a mobile number, not the issuer's official line
card offer seen in a social media ad followed by a call
typical_claims: you are eligible for a credit limit increase today
we will waive your annual fee if you verify now
your new card needs activation; share the OTP
fill this form to get a lifetime-free card with lounge access
pay Re 1 to confirm your card upgrade
coaching_phrases: fill in the 'form' (actually an APK) sent on WhatsApp while the caller waits
red_flag_questions: Did someone offer to increase your card limit, waive a fee or activate a card over the phone?
Were you asked to install a form or app sent on WhatsApp?
Were you asked to approve a Re 1 or small payment, or share an OTP or CVV?
Did the offer start from a social media ad?
cues_en: they said my limit will be doubled
cues_hinglish: card activate karna hai otp batao

first_seen.value: by 2022 (RBI BE(A)WARE and 'Raju and the Forty Thieves' booklets)

trend.note: RBI lists annual-fee waiver, card activation and limit upgradation frauds among its forty stories; APK-based card-offer fraud reported Nov 2025. No cited statistics.

official_truth: Banks and genuine financial institutions never ask for OTP, PIN, CVV or passwords, and card issuers never ask you to install third-party apps; limit, fee and card requests should be made only through the issuer's official app, website or helpline.
advice: Ignore unsolicited limit, fee-waiver or upgrade calls
Make card requests only via the issuer's app, website or number on the card
Never install files sent on WhatsApp or share OTP/CVV
Block the card and call 1930 if details were shared
applicability_note: Usually credential/OTP or malware theft where the fraudster transacts; only token 'verification' payments are victim-initiated.

name_en: Fake customer care / refund helpline (search, maps, social media)
summary: Fraudsters plant fake customer-care numbers for banks, insurers, Aadhaar centres and online services in search results, or watch for complaints on social media and call the complainant posing as support. To process a 'refund' or fix a failed transaction they send fake complaint portals, ask for card number, CVV, expiry or OTP, push screen-sharing or SMS-forwarding apps, or send UPI requests that the victim is told to approve with their PIN to 'receive' money.
victim_profile: People seeking help with a failed transaction, refund, booking or service complaint; RBI notes those new to digital payments are especially at risk.
indicators: helpline number found via search engine, maps or social media
'customer care' number is a 10-digit mobile number
call arrives right after you complained publicly on social media
refund requires card number, CVV, OTP or a link/portal
asked to enter UPI PIN or scan a QR code to 'receive' a refund
asked to install AnyDesk, a support app or an SMS-forwarding app
typical_claims: I am calling from customer care about your complaint
to process your refund, fill this complaint form with your card details
enter your UPI PIN to receive the refund
install this app so I can help you get your money back
your failed transaction will be reversed once you share the OTP
coaching_phrases: enter your UPI PIN to receive the refund (receiving money never needs a PIN)
type your card details into the complaint portal while on the call
red_flag_questions: Where did you get this customer care number: from the official website or app, or from a search result or social media?
Are you being asked to enter your UPI PIN or scan a QR code to receive a refund?
Has the 'support' person asked you to install an app or share card details or OTP?
Did they contact you after you posted a complaint online?
cues_en: refund will come to your account
cues_hinglish: customer care ka number google se liya
qr scan karo paise wapas aayenge
complaint form bharo card details ke saath
paisa wapas aa jayega otp batao

trend.note: Documented by RBI (2022) and CloudSEK-reported fake complaint portals (Moneylife, Jul 2022); no cited statistics.

official_truth: RBI advises taking customer-care numbers only from official websites, notes customer care numbers are never mobile numbers, and reminds that receiving money never requires entering a UPI PIN or scanning a QR code.
advice: Get helpline numbers only from the official website or app
Never enter UPI PIN or scan a QR code to receive money
Never install apps or share card/OTP details for a refund
Report to 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in
applicability_note: UPI 'collect'/PIN-to-receive and QR payments are victim-approved and holdable; card/OTP capture and remote-access variants are not.

name_en: Pensioner life certificate / pension office impersonation
summary: During the annual life-certificate season, callers posing as the pension department or CPAO contact pensioners, quote their PPO number, retirement date, Aadhaar and nominee details to sound genuine, and say the life certificate must be updated online or the pension will be affected. They ask for an OTP or personal details 'to update the certificate' and then take over and drain the pension account.
victim_profile: Senior-citizen pensioners, especially elderly or unwell people who find it hard to visit a bank branch (Moneylife 2022; CPAO notice).
indicators: call claiming to be from the pension office, treasury or CPAO
caller already knows PPO number, retirement date or Aadhaar
says the life certificate must be updated by phone or online now
asks for an OTP, bank details or personal information
warns the pension will stop if you do not act
typical_claims: I am calling from the pension department about your life certificate
your life certificate is not updated; your pension will stop
tell me the OTP to update your life certificate online
we have your PPO number; just confirm your details
red_flag_questions: Did someone call you saying they are from the pension office or CPAO about your life certificate?
Have they asked you for an OTP or bank details?
Did they say your pension will stop if you do not act now?
Has anyone asked you to transfer money or approve a payment for your pension?
cues_en: they said my pension will be stopped
cues_hinglish: pension office se bol raha hoon

first_seen.value: by November 2022 (CPAO warning reported by Moneylife)

trend.note: CPAO still carries an 'Attention Pensioners' warning on its home page (Oct 2026); no cited statistics.

official_truth: CPAO does not call pensioners for life certificate submission or ask for personal information or OTPs; life certificates are given at the bank or through the Aadhaar-based Jeevan Pramaan facility.
advice: Never share OTP or pension/bank details on a call
Submit life certificate only at your bank or via Jeevan Pramaan
Warn elderly relatives about these calls
Report to the bank and 1930 immediately
applicability_note: OTP capture lets fraudsters move pension money themselves; Ruko can warn pensioners but rarely hold.

name_en: Mobile tower installation / lease fee scam
summary: Fraudsters promise property owners high monthly rent and a lump-sum advance for installing a mobile tower on their land or rooftop, then demand upfront payments described as government tax under the Telecom Act, registration, NOC or security fees, backed by forged TRAI/DoT letters and fake No Objection Certificates. After collecting money they become unreachable.
victim_profile: Owners of land, rooftops or premises seeking rental income; no further profile documented.
indicators: unsolicited offer of high rent for installing a mobile tower
upfront 'government tax', registration, NOC or security fee
letter or NOC claiming to be from TRAI, DoT or the Ministry of Communications
payment to a personal or private company account
pressure to pay quickly to 'book' the site
typical_claims: your property is approved for a mobile tower with high monthly rent
pay the government tax under the Telecom Act to proceed
here is your NOC from TRAI/DoT; pay the processing fee
you will receive a large advance once the security deposit is paid
red_flag_questions: Is this payment for a mobile tower installation, lease agreement, NOC or 'government tax'?
Did the offer come through a call, ad or website rather than directly from a telecom operator?
Were you shown a letter or NOC from TRAI or DoT?
Is the money going to a personal or private account?
cues_hinglish: security deposit bharo tower ke liye

trend.note: Still listed in TRAI's August 2025 advisory on frauds misusing its identity; no cited statistics.

official_truth: TRAI is not involved in any tax or fee on leasing premises for mobile towers and does not issue No Objection Certificates for them.
advice: Do not pay any upfront tax, NOC or registration fee for a tower
Verify directly with the telecom operator through its official channels
Treat TRAI/DoT letters demanding payment as forged
Report to 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in
applicability_note: The victim personally transfers upfront fees, often in several instalments, which Ruko can hold and question.

name_en: AePS biometric (cloned fingerprint) withdrawal
summary: Fraudsters harvest Aadhaar numbers and fingerprints (for example from property registration documents downloaded from state registration websites, or captured during Aadhaar updates), make silicone or polymer fingerprint clones, and use AePS business-correspondent devices or apps to withdraw money from linked bank accounts without any OTP. Victims often notice only when balances fall, sometimes in accounts they rarely use.
victim_profile: Holders of Aadhaar-linked bank accounts, including property buyers/sellers whose registration documents are online and senior citizens with little-used accounts (Moneylife 2022, 2023).
indicators: cash withdrawals via AePS or a business correspondent that you did not make
debits without any OTP or card use
fingerprints captured by an agent during an Aadhaar update or enrolment
property registration documents with your fingerprints are available online
withdrawals from an account you rarely use
typical_claims: (no caller script; victim reports) money was withdrawn through a bank mitra / customer service point without any OTP
(victim reports) I never used that account but cash was withdrawn with my Aadhaar
red_flag_questions: Have you seen cash withdrawals you did not make, without any OTP?
Did an agent take your fingerprints recently for an Aadhaar update or other form?
Are your Aadhaar biometrics locked?
Was any money withdrawn through a banking correspondent or customer service point?
cues_en: they withdrew money using my thumb
cues_hinglish: bina otp ke paise nikal gaye

trend.note: Cyberabad gang withdrew Rs 14.64 lakh from 149 customers (2022); national cybercrime portal warned of OTP-less AePS fraud (reported 2023). No national statistics cited.

official_truth: The national cybercrime portal advises Aadhaar holders to lock their biometrics through the UIDAI website or app so they cannot be used for AePS withdrawals without unlocking.
advice: Lock Aadhaar biometrics on the UIDAI website or app and unlock only when needed
Give fingerprints only at authorised Aadhaar or bank centres
Check SMS alerts and passbooks for AePS withdrawals
Report to the bank and 1930 immediately
applicability_note: Money leaves through cloned-biometric AePS withdrawals with no victim-initiated transfer; Ruko can only warn and advise biometric locking.

name_en: Fake customs officer: pay duty to release a held gift or parcel
summary: Fraudsters posing as Indian Customs (often after a social-media or matrimonial contact says they sent a costly gift, or claims to be detained at the airport) say a parcel or person is held and demand 'customs duty', clearance or penalty payments into a personal bank account. The parcel never arrives and the demands escalate until the victim stops paying.
victim_profile: People contacted through social media and matrimonial sites who are promised gifts from abroad (Moneylife, Aug 2023); no further profile documented.
indicators: call or SMS from 'customs' about a gift or parcel you did not order
demand to pay duty into a personal or individual bank account
overseas friend or match says a gift is stuck at customs
repeated new charges after the first payment
no Document Identification Number (DIN) on the communication
typical_claims: a costly gift from abroad is held at customs; pay the duty to release it
your friend has been detained at the airport and needs money for customs
pay the clearance charge today or the parcel will be confiscated
transfer the duty to this officer's account
red_flag_questions: Is this payment customs duty for a gift or parcel someone else sent you?
Is the account a personal account rather than an official government payment channel?
Did the request come from someone you met online or a caller claiming to be customs?
Does the notice have a DIN you can verify on the CBIC website?

trend.note: No statistics cited.

official_truth: Indian Customs does not call or send SMS asking for customs duty to be paid into a personal account, and genuine customs communications carry a DIN that can be verified on the CBIC website.
advice: Never pay 'customs duty' into a personal account
Verify any notice's DIN on the CBIC website
Stop contact with online friends who need money for a gift
Report to 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in
applicability_note: Victim personally transfers 'duty' payments, often repeatedly, which Ruko can hold.

name_en: Fake RBI official: release of lottery / foreign funds / bonus after fees
summary: Letters, emails, SMS or calls using RBI-like letterheads, fake websites or the names of real RBI officials tell victims that lottery winnings, funds from abroad or other payouts are waiting, and ask for small 'processing', tax-clearance, conversion or clearing fees into specified bank accounts, followed by ever larger demands. Impostors posing as RBI officials have also used insurance-bonus stories to extract large sums.
victim_profile: General public; documented victims include an 82-year-old retired professor (Moneylife 2022).
indicators: message or call claiming RBI holds money or a payout for you
letter signed in the name of an RBI official with a contact number
fees for processing, tax clearance or currency conversion before release
payments to accounts of individuals or proprietary firms
fake website resembling RBI's
typical_claims: RBI has approved release of your foreign remittance; pay the conversion charges
you have won a lottery; RBI will release the funds after tax clearance
I am a deputy general manager at RBI handling your payout
deposit the processing fee in this account to receive your funds
red_flag_questions: Has someone said RBI is holding money, a prize or a payout for you?
Are you paying a fee, tax or charge before the money is released?
Is the receiving account in an individual's or private firm's name?
Have you already paid once and been asked for more?
cues_en: they said rbi will release my money

first_seen.value: by 2012 (RBI says it had cautioned the public on several earlier occasions)

trend.note: Long-running; no recent statistics cited.

official_truth: RBI never contacts the public by unsolicited calls or emails asking for money or personal information, does not hold accounts for or pay money to individuals, and does not communicate lottery or foreign-fund offers.
advice: Ignore any offer of funds 'held by RBI'
Never pay fees to release a prize or remittance
Check that RBI websites end in rbi.org.in
Report to local police, 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in
applicability_note: Victims push repeated fee transfers themselves, which Ruko can hold and question.

name_en: Fake police / I4C / CBI legal notice email
summary: Emails with PDF 'notices' bearing logos of CBI, IB, I4C or a Commissioner of Police and fake 'top secret' stamps accuse recipients of visiting illegal sites or offences involving minors and demand a reply within 24-48 hours to avoid arrest or court action. They are sent in bulk from non-government domains; replying opens the door to extortion or a digital-arrest style follow-up.
victim_profile: Random recipients from email lists; documented recipients include a student (Moneylife 2024).
indicators: email or PDF notice citing a court order for viewing illegal content
logos of several agencies and 'certified'/'top secret' stamps
deadline of 24-48 hours to respond
sender domain is not a government (.gov.in/.nic.in) address
poor translation or emojis in the subject line
typical_claims: a court order has been issued against you for visiting illegal websites
respond within 48 hours or face serious legal action
this is an official warning from the Commissioner of Police
reply to this official court order warning
red_flag_questions: Did you receive an email notice accusing you of a crime and asking you to reply or pay?
Is the sender address a government domain?
Are you being asked to pay a fine or settlement to close the case?
Has anyone followed up by phone or video call about this notice?
cues_en: they emailed me a police notice
cues_hinglish: police ka notice email pe aaya

trend.note: Reported again as recurring in Aug 2024; no statistics cited.

official_truth: PIB Fact Check has confirmed that such I4C/police notice emails are fake and that no Government of India agency sends them.
advice: Do not reply, pay or open attachments
Check the sender domain; government mail uses official domains
Report the email to cybercrime.gov.in or 1930
Do not take follow-up calls demanding settlement
applicability_note: Sources document only the notice and reply demand; any later payment demand (not documented here) would be victim-initiated and holdable.
